Tune Over `alpha` for Every Split of a Resample

Source: R/survival_metrics.R
tune_alpha_by_split.Rd

Evaluates candidate `(split, alpha)` (or `(split, formula)`) combinations as a single flat task grid across all available [future::plan()] workers and row-binds the successful fits.

Usage

tune_alpha_by_split(
  object,
  ...,
  num_alpha_values = 10,
  num_fixed = 6,
  alphas = NULL,
  formulas = NULL,
  progress = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  calibrate = TRUE,
  checkpoint_dir = NULL,
  checkpoint_mismatch = c("recompute", "overwrite", "error"),
  shard = NULL,
  chunk_size = NULL,
  on_complete = getOption("templecbe.on_complete", NULL),
  .fn_name = "tune_alpha_by_split"
)

Arguments

object

A resampling object with a `splits` column (e.g. one element of the `inner_resamples` column of [rsample::nested_cv()]).

...

Arguments passed to [glmnet_IBS()] (`recipe`, `feature_names`, `time_data`, `id_col`, `cox.ties`, ...).

num_alpha_values

Total number of `alpha` values in the grid.

num_fixed

Number of evenly spaced values from 0 to 1 in the grid.

alphas

Optional numeric vector of `alpha` values to use instead of the generated grid; in formula mode, one per formula.

formulas

Optional character vector of `+`-separated feature sets, or a list of one-sided formulas, each fit as a separate model (see [glmnet_IBS()]'s `formula`).

progress

Show a progress bar.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducible random draws across splits.

calibrate

Logical (default TRUE); whether to benchmark baseline serial execution. Set to FALSE to skip serial benchmarking and dispatch tasks directly to parallel workers.

checkpoint_dir

Optional directory path to save checkpoint files. Finished splits/tasks are loaded from disk on rerun when their fingerprint matches, skipping recomputation.

checkpoint_mismatch

Action when an existing checkpoint file's fingerprint does not match the current inputs/settings: `"recompute"` (default; warns and recomputes), `"overwrite"` (overwrites mismatched files in place and removes stale checkpoints from previous runs), or `"error"` (stops immediately).

shard

Optional integer vector `c(i, n)` specifying that this call should process shard `i` of `n` across machines into `checkpoint_dir`. Use [collect_checkpoints()] to merge all shards once finished.

chunk_size

Optional positive integer passed to [furrr::furrr_options()] controlling the number of tasks batched per worker invocation. Defaults to `NULL` (one chunk per worker so each worker receives all of its assigned tasks in a single batch).

on_complete

Optional callback `function(result)` (or option `templecbe.on_complete`) invoked when the run finishes or errors.

.fn_name

Internal caller function name for logging and checkpointing metadata.

Value

A tibble of [glmnet_IBS()] results with an `inner_resamples_splits` column giving the split's identifier.

Nested Parallelism, Benchmarking & Physical Cores

When tuning penalized survival models across nested resampling structures, computation scales multiplicatively: \(\text{outer folds} \times \text{inner splits} \times \text{alphas} \times \text{internal CV folds}\). `tune_alpha_by_split()` flattens `inner splits x alphas` into a single task pool (e.g. 7 splits x 10 alphas = 70 tasks), sends the shared dataset, recipe, and split definitions once per worker, and pre-preps/bakes each split once per worker rather than repeating recipe preprocessing for every `alpha`.

**Physical Cores vs. Hyper-Threading:** When configuring a parallel backend (e.g. `future::plan(future::multisession, workers = ...)`), it is strongly recommended to set worker count to the number of *physical* CPU cores ([parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)]), leaving 1–2 cores for the coordinator process and OS I/O, rather than using all hyper-threaded logical cores. Because CPU-intensive coordinate descent and Breslow hazard calculations saturate CPU execution units and L1/L2 caches, two worker processes executing on siblings of the same physical core contend for the same ALUs, FPUs, and memory bandwidth, which frequently doubles per-task compute latency inside concurrent workers (e.g., tasks taking ~2.2 s serially taking ~5.0 s inside 14 concurrent workers on 8 physical cores). Sizing workers to physical cores yields optimal wall-clock speedup and reduces IPC contention. Set future::plan(multisession, workers = 7) before calling while keeping inner model evaluations sequential (parallel = FALSE in glmnet_IBS()). Use `chunk_size` to control how many tasks are batched per worker message.
